# Norman Douglas

## Overview

- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v5 c15 P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031), [v5 c21 P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v5 c35 P7](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0007)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** old reprobate  <sub>[v5 c16 P77](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0077)</sub>

## Appearance

Norman Douglas is a big, fine-looking man with a broad chest, a massive head, and a high, white, unwrinkled forehead. He has a mane of red hair ungrizzled by age, a long red beard, and flashing blue eyes. In his youth, he was described as a handsome, red-haired giant.

_Sources: [v5 c16 P28](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0028), [v5 c21 P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015), [v5 c32 P2](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0002)_

## Personality

Norman Douglas is a blustering, loud, and noisy individual whose personality dominates any room he enters. He is short-tempered, bad-tempered, and prone to bullying those who show meekness, yet he genuinely admires spirit and spunk in others. Despite his intimidating exterior, he can be amiable, bracing, stimulating, and generous. He possesses a clever, well-read mind and a sharp, humorous wit, though he is entirely indifferent to whether people dislike him.

_Sources: [v5 c15 P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031), [v5 c16 P27](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0027), [v5 c16 P28](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0028), [v5 c16 P29](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0029), [v5 c16 P87](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0087), [v5 c22 P1](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0001), [v5 c26 P19](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0019), [v5 c26 P21](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0021), [v5 c32 P1](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0001), [v5 c32 P2](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0002), [v5 c34 P6](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0006)_

## History

In his youth, Norman Douglas courted Ellen West for two years before a quarrel led to their separation. In a fit of temper, Norman married Hester Reese to spite Ellen, but he despised Hester's meekness and broke what little spirit she had. After a dispute over a cow deal with a church session member, he refused to attend church for twenty years. Ten years after burying his wife, Norman was visited by Faith Meredith, whose spirited temper during a disagreement over church attendance earned his respect and convinced him to return to church services. Upon returning to church, he saw Ellen West again and fell in love with her once more. He began attending social gatherings and courting Ellen publicly, engaging in persistent bullying and coaxing until they agreed to marry.

_Sources: [v5 c15 P29](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0029), [v5 c15 P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031), [v5 c16 P27](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0027), [v5 c16 P60](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0060), [v5 c17 P0](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0000), [v5 c17 P1](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0001), [v5 c22 P1](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0001), [v5 c26 P17](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0017), [v5 c34 P6](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0006), [v5 c35 P7](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0007)_

## Quotes

> Give me a spunky woman—spunk for me every time.  <sub>[v5 c15 P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031)</sub>

> A good squall clears the air and briskens things up. But no drizzling and fogging afterwards—no drizzling and fogging, woman. I can’t stand that. Temper in a woman but no tears for me.  <sub>[v5 c16 P61](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0061)</sub>

> You tell him that if he wants to keep me in good humour to preach a good rip-roaring sermon on hell once every six months—and the more brimstone the better. I like ‘em smoking.  <sub>[v5 c16 P77](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0077)</sub>

> She wasn’t very well just before I buried her ten years ago, but I reckon she has better health now  <sub>[v5 c17 P1](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0001)</sub>

> She’s that full of spunk she’s bursting with it. And all the old grannies want to tame her, darn them. But they’ll never be able to do it—never!  <sub>[v5 c26 P19](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0019)</sub>
